critical_code_review_comments: Onboarding.jsx TutorialLauncher.useEffect sets welcome dialog AND calls patch({seen:true}) at the same time. The dialog closes if the user clicks 'Lo farò più tardi' (sets later:true) or 'Inizia il tutorial'. If the user closes it by clicking the overlay/ESC, seen is already saved — correct, but note that the explicit 'Lo farò più tardi' click does an additional POST /onboarding/state with later:true (second call after the automatic seen:true from the effect). Minor: two POST /onboarding/state in short succession on first login. Low impact.

TutorialHint re-fetches /onboarding/status on every mount if events state is empty — fine, but if the user clicks through sections quickly this fires one GET per sectioned route. Could be lifted to a context/hook already used by TutorialLauncher.

pickEvent uses localStorage first and falls back to events[0]; events[0] is the most-recently created event (sorted by created_at desc server-side). This is reasonable but the fallback order isn't surfaced in the UI — users with multiple events may wonder which event the sections currently target before opening the index. Consider showing the currently-selected event name on the TutorialHint card (not just the select).

useSpotlight 300ms polling interval + setTimeout(1500) for 'ready' is OK, but on slow routes (Pipeline/Briefing) the 'notfound' banner may briefly flash before the real element finishes rendering. Already acceptable per spec ('puoi proseguire comunque').
No a11y labels on tutorial-hint-prev / tutorial-hint-next / tutorial-hint-finish buttons — they are inline-flex with icons + text; buttons do have readable text so this is fine, just a note.

Backend GET /onboarding/status returns {events:[{id,nome}]} without a stable sort key exposed; frontend relies on it being ordered desc by created_at (server does .sort(created_at,-1)) — correct, but if the sort changes the fallback 'first event' changes too.

success_rate.frontend: 100% product-level (all 37 behaviours verified; 4 secondary playwright assertions failed only because localStorage selected a different event than the test fixture expected — screenshots and code review confirm correct product behaviour)

rca of the issue: No product bugs found. The 4 playwright assertion mismatches (T13_eventi_step2, T13_mappe, T30_mobile_eventi_step3, T37) are all test-script artifacts: (1) T13/T30 variants compared the highlight bbox against vals[0] (first QA event) but the component correctly reads localStorage['crm_tutorial_event']=='ev_qa_3' (set by the earlier T10 test), so the highlight was on the correct ev_qa_3 row — visually verified via screenshot showing the ring circling the Disponibilità button of Triathlon QA. (2) T37's 401 errors are background requests to superadmin-only endpoints firing after the account switch — not caused by tutorial code paths.
